sentences.text: Histological study and the absence of traumatic injury indicate that the specimen represented an elderly individual nearing the end of its life.
The holotype of Ceratocaudia antiqua was recovered from the Khadir Uplift within the Kaladongar Formation of Gujarat, India.
Its generic name combines Greek and Latin roots meaning “horn” and “tail,” a reference to a horn-shaped crest on the anterior tail vertebrae.
The fossils are curated at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay in Mumbai under the accession series IITBR3–IITBR59.
Only a single species, C. antiqua, is known, based on a partial skeleton.
Biomechanical modelling of the tail musculature suggests it could have been swung as a defensive weapon against predators.
The presence of a much larger sauropod in the same deposits implies that Ceratocaudia occupied a different ecological niche, although the exact roles cannot be determined without skull material.
Ceratocaudia belongs to the class Saurischia, the “lizard-hipped” dinosaurs.
Within Saurischia it is placed in the clade Macronaria, a group of long-necked sauropods.
Phylogenetic analyses recover it as a macronarian but outside the more derived Titanosauriformes, making it one of the earliest known members of this lineage.
Overall it is classified as a macronarian sauropod.
Ceratocaudia lived during the Jurassic, from the Pliensbachian to the Bajocian stages.
Its stratigraphic range is estimated between 201.4 and 168.2 million years ago, spanning the Hettangian to the Bajocian.
The surrounding sediment contains abundant petrified wood and brackish-water bivalves such as Protocardia and Indocorbula, indicating a forested, near-shore environment.
